'''Trudy Rose Govier''' (born August 3, 1944) is a Canadian philosopher known for her work in [[informal logic]] and [[argumentation]]. She is the author of the influential text ''A Practical Study of Argument''. She has also been a frequent commentator in Canadian media on issues related to violence and conflict resolution.<ref name=Homepage>{{cite web|url=http://members.shaw.ca/govier/|title=Trudy Govier Homepage}}</ref>

==Career==

Govier received her PhD in philosophy from the [[University of Waterloo]] in 1971. She has taught philosophy at [[Trent University]], [[Simon Fraser University]], the [[University of Amsterdam]], the [[University of Calgary]], the [[University of Lethbridge]], and the [[University of Winnipeg]].<ref name=Homepage /> Much of Govier's work has surrounded practical argument, focusing on issues of trust, forgiveness, and reconciliation. She has been a distinguished visiting researcher with the [[Centre for Research in Reasoning, Argumentation, and Rhetoric]] at the [[University of Windsor]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.uwindsor.ca/crrar/past-visiting-researchers|title=CRRAR Visiting Researchers}}</ref> She retired from teaching in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uleth.ca/artsci/news/2012/12/professor-trudy-govier-retires|title=Trudy Govier Retires}}</ref>

The nature of Govier's approach to argumentation has prompted her to engage practically with social issues outside of academia. She is a founding member of the Calgary chapter of the peace activist organization [[Project Ploughshares]]<ref name=Homepage /> and has been involved in labour advocacy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/support-sought-for-calgary-herald-strikers-1.234979|title=CBC News: Support sought for Calgary Herald strikers}}</ref>

== Selected works ==

*''A Practical Study of Argument, 7th Edition'' (Belmont: Wadsworth, 2012)
*''Taking Wrongs Seriously: Acknowledgement, Reconciliation, and the Politics of Sustainable Peace'' (Amherst, NY: Humanity Books, 2006)
*''A Delicate Balance: What Philosophy Can Tell Us About Terrorism'' (Boulder, CO: Westview Press, 2002)
*''Forgiveness and Revenge'' (London: Routledge, 2002)
*''The Philosophy of Argument'' (Newport News, VA: Vale Press, 1999)
*''Dilemmas of Trust'' (Montreal & Kingston: McGill-Queen's University Press, 1998)
*''Social Trust and Human Communities'' Montreal & Kingston: McGill-Queen's University Press, 1997)
*''Socrates' Children'' (Peterborough, ON: Broadview Press, 1997)
*''God, the Devil, and the Perfect Pizza.'' (Peterborough, ON: Broadview Press, 1989)
*''Problems in Argument Evaluation and Analysis'' (Dordrecht, NL and Berlin: Foris/deGruyter, 1987)
